AK-governor.statusNote: Open seat: Gov. Mike Dunleavy is term-limited and cannot seek a third consecutive term. In the Aug 18 top-four primary, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D), who represented Sitka and Southeast Alaska in the Legislature for a decade, and former Anchorage state Sen. Tom Begich (D) lead with about 22% and 20%. Conservative activist and business owner Bernadette Wilson (R) holds third at about 10%. The fourth spot is not settled: former Anchorage Mayor Dave Bronson (R) leads a tight pack, with certification expected Aug 31. The November general uses ranked choice voting. Certified fourth-spot correction, Sep 2 2026: Tom Begich (D), who finished second in the Aug 18 primary, officially withdrew Aug 31; the app's advancing list should have him REMOVED (fragment format cannot remove ids). That promoted Bernadette Wilson to second and Dave Bronson to third. The fourth slot was Treg Taylor's until Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom disqualified him Aug 31 for incomplete financial disclosures; his running mate Candice English took his spot on the ticket with Jodi Taylor (Treg's wife) as her new running mate. As of Sep 1, Alaska's News Source still described English's ticket status as pending compliance review of Jodi Taylor's disclosure, with a possible further shuffle to sixth- or seventh-place finishers if she is also disqualified. Certified final four for the November ranked-choice general as of Sep 2, 2026: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D, 22.5%), Bernadette Wilson (R, 10.1%), Dave Bronson (R, 8.1%), Candice English (R, pending).
